title: Backtest Your Agent Against Yesterday's Web — Ryan Ahern, Exa
talk_summary: Exa presents Snapshot, a versioned web-search capability that lets agents search the web as it existed at a past date, mainly to backtest predictive systems without future-information leakage. The practical lesson is less about Exa and more about rigorous historical replay: freeze the information available at decision time, test features one at a time, and keep a holdout set to catch overfitting.

takeaways.what_they_do: They replay an agent against a past snapshot so it only sees information available before the outcome, and they explicitly warn that visible test sets get overfit without a holdout.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can constrain like what particular information is exposed at which time

takeaways.technique: Freeze repo before known PR solve
takeaways.what_they_do: They freeze a repo state just before a PR was solved, let the coding system run, and check whether it can resolve the task without future information leaking in.
takeaways.evidence_quote: freeze right before that PR was solved uh in an in an external repo and then let the system run

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that versioned backtests let you prove an agentic feature adds value rather than relying on vibes, and you can tune search behavior against true outcomes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prove that it adds value, not just like vibes and hope that it adds value

takeaways.technique: Feature ablation one check at a time
takeaways.what_they_do: They test individual yes/no features against true positives and false positives, then combine them only after seeing whether each feature improves or worsens the score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: add it into your system like one feature at a time

takeaways.what_they_do: Exa says it returns just the tokens needed across results so the downstream agent does not pay large input-token costs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: return just the tokens that you need
